verdict.summary: OAuth apps are self-serve in a free Developer Portal with no documented review, so any BambooHR customer can authorize your app once you register a redirect URI and pick scopes. The catches are that there's no sandbox until you're accepted into the Marketplace partner program (which needs 100+ customers), scopes are still in beta, and rate limits aren't published.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Assumes you already have access to a BambooHR company to test against. Without one, add time to get a trial or a customer's test account, because BambooHR provides sandboxes only to Marketplace partners.

timeToProd.assumes: An unlisted OAuth app reading employee data, connected by customers who enter their company domain; Marketplace listing is optional and only for companies with 100+ customers.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Nothing — no review documented for unlisted OAuth apps. Marketplace listing waits on Partner Team review with no published timeline.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: BambooHR says 'Anyone can build an integration using the BambooHR API'. Neither BambooHR nor third-party setup guides mention an app approval step, but BambooHR doesn't state outright that there's none.

verdict.cost: Free Developer Portal account. A Marketplace listing requires a signed partner agreement; no fees are published.

prerequisites.item: A free BambooHR Developer Portal account
prerequisites.why: OAuth client ID, client secret, redirect URIs and scopes are all managed there.

prerequisites.item: Access to a BambooHR company to test against
prerequisites.why: The authorize and token endpoints live on each customer's company subdomain, and BambooHR provides sandbox accounts only after you join the Marketplace Partner Program.

prerequisites.item: For a Marketplace listing: 100+ total customers, a security questionnaire, and the Marketplace Partner Agreement
prerequisites.why: These are the stated eligibility requirements for the Marketplace program.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP or HITRUST are preferred, not required.

scopeTiers.impact: offline_access is the only way to get a refresh token; without it users must re-authorize about every hour.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Scope names beyond offline_access come from a third-party guide (Unified).

scopeTiers.tier: Basic employee directory and org data
scopeTiers.impact: Enough for an HR helper agent that looks up people, managers and time off. Each scope can be set to No Access, Read or Read/Write in the portal.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: BambooHR's scopes page is in beta and lists no scopes; names are from Unified's setup guide.

scopeTiers.impact: No separate review is documented, but customers see these on the consent screen and the connecting user's own BambooHR permissions still limit what is returned.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Scope names from a third-party guide; the absence of extra review is our inference.

scopeTiers.impact: Lets an agent update records or file time-off requests. Request only what you need; customers' admins see the list.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Exact write-scope strings should be confirmed in the Developer Portal.

steps.title: Create a Developer Portal account
steps.detail: Sign up for a free account at the BambooHR Developer Portal.

steps.title: Add an application
steps.detail: On the Applications page select Add application, name it, then copy the Client ID, Client Secret and Application Key.

steps.title: Register the redirect URI and select scopes
steps.detail: Add your exact HTTPS callback under Redirect URIs, then under Application Scopes pick No Access, Read or Read/Write per category, and add offline_access under Miscellaneous.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Exact-match redirect requirement is official; UI labels are from third-party guides.

steps.title: Draft the minimal scope list
steps.detail: Map each agent feature to the fields it needs and pick the narrowest scope per category, checking field-to-scope mappings shown in the portal.

steps.title: Build the domain-aware OAuth flow
steps.detail: Ask the user for their company subdomain, redirect to https://{companyDomain}.bamboohr.com/authorize.php?request=authorize with response_type=code, scopes joined by '+', and state, then exchange at https://{companyDomain}.bamboohr.com/token.php?request=token.

steps.title: Test against a real BambooHR company
steps.detail: Authorize with a test or customer account and confirm the consent screen lists the expected scopes and that fields come back.

steps.title: Add backoff and refresh handling
steps.detail: Refresh before the 1-hour expiry, store the newest refresh token, and retry 429/503 with exponential backoff and jitter, honoring Retry-After when present.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Rate-limit behavior from a third-party engineering guide.

steps.title: Optionally apply to the Marketplace
steps.detail: If you have 100+ customers, submit the partner application, complete the security questionnaire, sign the agreement, and submit a listing with docs, logo, images, help guide and demo URL.

steps.title: Wait for Marketplace Partner Team review
steps.detail: The Partner Team reviews and follows up; no timeline is published. Not needed for unlisted OAuth.

agentCanDo: Build the per-subdomain authorize and token exchange code
Batch employee field requests under the 400-field cap
Draft Marketplace listing docs and help guide
humanMustDo: Create the Developer Portal account and app
Copy the client secret into your secret store
Provide a BambooHR company to test against

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails with a redirect error
blockers.cause: redirect_uri differs from the registered one, even by a trailing slash or letter case.
blockers.fix: Register and send the exact same URI.

blockers.symptom: No refresh_token in the token response; users must reconnect every hour
blockers.cause: offline_access scope wasn't requested or assigned.
blockers.fix: Add offline_access in the portal and include it in the scope parameter.

blockers.symptom: Authorize URL redirects to bamboohr.com homepage or API returns 404
blockers.fix: Ask the customer for their exact subdomain and store it as editable config.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: https://example.bamboohr.com/authorize.php?request=authorize returned 302 to http://www.bamboohr.com/ for a non-existent company.

blockers.symptom: Fields silently missing from employee responses
blockers.cause: Scope or the authorizing user's BambooHR permissions don't cover those fields; the API omits them without error.
blockers.fix: Add the right scope and have a user with sufficient access authorize.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Described for API keys in a third-party guide; we infer the same for OAuth.

blockers.symptom: Can't use OpenID Connect Login API to fetch an API key for new customers
blockers.cause: BambooHR closed that method to new integrations.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: A third-party guide dates the deprecation to April 14, 2025; BambooHR's page gives no date.

blockers.fix: Back off exponentially with jitter and spread syncs over time.

nuances.text: Access tokens expire after 3600 seconds; refresh tokens are only issued with offline_access and their lifetime isn't documented.
Every customer has its own subdomain for authorize, token and API calls, so your connect flow must collect it before redirecting.
OAuth scopes are labeled beta and 'in active development'; scope names and field coverage may change.
OAuth fixes a classic API-key problem: keys are tied to a person and break when that user leaves, while app scopes are visible to customers before install.
A single Get Employee request is capped at 400 fields.
Marketplace partners must answer leads within 1 business day and support customers using the integration.
